calls.head: The Bruins can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Bruins’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Mammoth’s power play is one of the league’s best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Bruins tonight.
calls.call: The Mammoth’s power play creates at least their usual 8.4 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Utah 5th for power play (8.4 expected goals per 60) · Boston 27th for penalty kill

calls.happened: Utah’s power play created 5.2 expected goals per 60 in 13:47 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.4, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: Sheltered against exposed
calls.body: The Bruins are near the top of the league for preventing dangerous shots, at the sheltered end; the Mammoth are one of the league’s worst, at the exposed end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Bruins prevent dangerous shots better than the Mammoth do.

BOS.head: We gave Boston a 40% chance, and Boston proved us wrong.

UTA.head: We gave Utah a 60% chance, but Boston had other ideas.

surprises.head: J. Swayman stole one
surprises.body: J. Swayman allowed 1 goal on shots worth 4.7 expected goals, 3.7 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 250 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Boston won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, Utah wins 82. Boston won anyway.

surprises.head: Utah got the good looks
surprises.body: Utah’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: The Bruins roll past the Mammoth
paras: The Bruins had this one put away early. Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring midway through the first. David Pastrnak added two power-play goals. Five different Bruins scored. Utah pulled Karel Vejmelka after three goals.

The score flatters the Bruins: the Mammoth had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Mammoth win about four in five. Jeremy Swayman made the difference in net, stopping 36 of 37.

items.text: David Pastrnak scored his first goal of the season.
